title: Herding End-to-End Autonomous Driving via Neuro-Symbolic Safety Guards
abstract: arXiv:2608.11451v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Modern end-to-end driving agents can achieve high average performance yet still violate basic traffic rules that a human driver would never miss. The reason is structural: they learn statistical patterns rather than the physical conditions that guarantee safe driving, leaving their decision-making process opaque and safety constraints unenforced. We introduce a neuro-symbolic safety guard, a lightweight module that attaches to the final command interface of an already-trained agent. Immediately before a command reaches the vehicle, it checks the command against explicit safety rules and, only when necessary, replaces it with the nearest safe alternative. Each intervention is directly executable and traceable to the rule that triggered it, while the guard itself requires no retraining and adds no learned component. Evaluated on the long-tail benchmarks Fail2Drive and Bench2Drive using the state-of-the-art TransFuser v6 (TFv6) as a case

translated_title: 通过神经符号安全护栏引导端到端自动驾驶
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.11451v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：现代端到端驾驶代理能够实现较高的平均性能，但仍会违反人类驾驶员绝不会忽略的基本交通规则。原因在于其结构性缺陷：它们学习的是统计模式，而非保证安全驾驶的物理条件，导致其决策过程不透明且安全约束无法强制执行。我们引入了一种神经符号安全护栏，这是一个轻量级模块，附加在已训练代理的最终命令接口上。在命令到达车辆之前，它会根据显式安全规则检查命令，并仅在必要时将其替换为最接近的安全替代方案。每次干预都可直接执行，并可追溯到触发该干预的规则，而护栏本身无需重新训练，也不添加任何学习组件。我们在长尾基准测试Fail2Drive和Bench2Drive上，以最先进的TransFuser v6（TFv6）作为案例进行了评估。
tldr: 本文提出一种神经符号安全护栏，通过轻量级、可追溯的规则检查，在不重新训练的情况下确保端到端自动驾驶系统遵守基本交通规则。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a neuro-symbolic safety guard that enforces basic traffic rule compliance in end-to-end autonomous driving via lightweight, traceable rule checks without retraining.
